label: early original-phase first occurrence of v/m/b/j/a/k after o/k/u/n/r-type context
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.9% of mass), at early positions t=1..5 (peak t=2-3), never at t=0, the delimiter, or in the copy phase. Input token is the main driver: v (8.9x lift, 33% of mass), m, b, j, then a, k; nearly silent on other tokens (u, d, h, digits). Almost always the first occurrence of that token. Magnitude rises when earlier inputs include o (strongest), k, u, n, r, p, j: top activations are v/j/b/m right after o o or o u. The context effect is graded rather than all-or-nothing, so a boolean predicate gets high mass recall (~0.86 dev) but low precision (~0.26). Most v/m/b/j/a/k inputs leave it inactive, especially late in the sequence or after unrelated prefixes.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: v, m, b, j; t=3: v, m, j, b; t=2: v, m, j, b) and the previous input (most: o, k, u, p, j, r; least: q, s, x, y); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, L=6 & t=7, t=2.
